title: Seoul Chili Pear Beef Cubes
seoTitle: Seoul Chili Pear Beef Cubes | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Gochujang beef skewers—sweet heat, fast char, not bulgogi night
subtitle: Korean chili paste glazed sirloin, sesame, and char for ten
description: Sirloin cubes marinate in gochujang, soy, and pear puree, grill on skewers with scallions until charred and 145°F, and finish with sesame and crushed peanuts.

steps.title: Build gochujang marinade
steps.instruction: Whisk gochujang, soy, pear puree, sesame oil, and garlic until smooth. Toss beef cubes and marinate at least 2 hours.

steps.title: Prep skewer station
steps.instruction: Soak wooden skewers if using. Line hotel pans with foil for holding. Have sesame and peanuts ready.

steps.title: Heat grill
steps.instruction: Preheat grill to medium-high, 450°F. Oil grates—gochujang sugar caramelizes fast.

steps.title: Thread skewers
steps.instruction: Alternate beef cubes and green onion pieces on skewers. Pat excess marinade off to reduce flare-ups.

steps.title: Grill in batches
steps.instruction: Grill skewers 3–4 minutes per side until charred and beef reads 140–145°F internal.

steps.title: Rest and hold
steps.instruction: Rest skewers 5 minutes. Slide beef and onions into hotel pans, cover with foil, hold at 170°F until service.

steps.title: Sesame finish
steps.instruction: Scatter sesame seeds and crushed peanuts over platters at the line—not before long hold.

steps.title: Tonight's line
steps.instruction: Serve two skewers per firefighter with steamed rice or lettuce wraps. Call temps: pull at 145°F, held at 170°F max.

proTips: Asian pear tenderizes beef—substitute grated apple if pear isn't available.
Leave gaps on skewers; packed cubes steam instead of charring.
Gochujang burns above 450°F—move to cooler zone if glaze darkens too fast.
tonightSpread: Gochujang beef skewers with sesame and crushed peanuts.
Quick kimchi slaw with rice vinegar.
leftovers: Chop beef into bibimbap-style rice bowls.
Stuff into lettuce wraps with extra gochujang.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Gochujang beef skewers hit a different lane than bulgogi platters. Beef cubes char fast, hold covered at 170°F, and eat well with rice or lettuce wraps.
mealPrepNotes: Marinate 2–6 hours. Grill medium-high 450°F in batches. Hold covered at 170°F up to 30 minutes. Sesame garnish at service only.
